definitions.explanation: A feeling of anger or irritation, often simmering or building up rather than an explosive outburst. Derived from the verb 腹立つ (to get angry).

examples.japanese: {腹立|はらだ}ちを{覚|おぼ}える。
{彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}に{腹立|はらだ}ちを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt annoyed by his attitude.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}を{何度|なんど}も{破|やぶ}られて、{腹立|はらだ}ちが{収|おさ}まらなかった。
examples.english: Having had promises broken repeatedly, my anger would not subside.

notes:
The noun form of {腹|はら}が{立|た}つ (to get angry, literally 'the belly rises'). Expresses anger that is felt internally, often building or simmering.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腹立|はらだ}ちを{覚|おぼ}える: to feel irritation/anger
- {腹立|はらだ}ちを{感|かん}じる: to feel annoyed
- {腹立|はらだ}ちが{収|おさ}まらない: anger won't subside
- {腹立|はらだ}ちを{抑|おさ}える: to hold back one's anger
- {腹立|はらだ}ちまぎれに: out of spite; in a fit of anger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {怒|いか}り: anger, wrath — stronger and more intense than {腹立|はらだ}ち
- {苛立|いらだ}ち: irritation, frustration — focuses on restless, fidgety irritation
- {立腹|りっぷく}: anger, indignation — more formal synonym; same kanji in different order
- {憤|いきどお}り: indignation, resentment — anger at something unjust

ETYMOLOGY:
From the Japanese body metaphor where the {腹|はら} (belly/gut) is the seat of emotions. When one is angry, the belly 'rises' ({立|た}つ).

cross_references.label: to get angry, to be irritated
